    1. compute(I)

Class Memoizer<I,O>

java.lang.Object
org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent.Memoizer<I,O>
Type Parameters:
I - The type of the input to the calculation
O - The type of the output of the calculation
All Implemented Interfaces:
Computable<I,O>
public class Memoizer<I,O> extends Object implements Computable<I,O>
Definition of an interface for a wrapper around a calculation that takes a single parameter and returns a result. The results for the calculation will be cached for future requests.

This is not a fully functional cache: it is unbounded, and there is no way of limiting or removing results once they have been generated. In particular, note the exception-caching default: unless the recalculate constructor option is set to true, the first exception thrown by a calculation for a given parameter is cached and rethrown for every future call with that parameter for the lifetime of this instance - a single transient failure permanently poisons that key. Set recalculate to true to retry failed calculations on subsequent calls instead.

Thanks go to Brian Goetz, Tim Peierls and the members of JCP JSR-166 Expert Group for coming up with the original implementation of the class. It was also published within Java Concurrency in Practice as a sample.

Since:
3.6

  • Method Details

    • compute

      public O compute(I arg) throws InterruptedException
      This method will return the result of the calculation and cache it, if it has not previously been calculated.

      This cache will also cache exceptions that occur during the computation if the recalculate parameter in the constructor was set to false, or not set: the first exception thrown for a given argument is rethrown for every future call with that argument. Otherwise, if an exception happened on the previous calculation, the method will attempt again to generate a value.

      The calculation for a given argument runs at most once per cached entry and executes outside any internal lock of the backing map (the pattern published in Java Concurrency in Practice): a slow calculation for one key does not block calls for unrelated keys, and a calculation may itself use this Memoizer without deadlocking. Concurrent callers for the same argument wait on the same Future.

      Specified by:
      compute in interface Computable<I,O>
      Parameters:
      arg - The argument for the calculation
      Returns:
      The result of the calculation
      Throws:
      InterruptedException - Thrown if the calculation is interrupted.
